description:
Each FIELD of a bitstring clause head is extracted TWICE per match: once by the
dispatch plan deciding whether the clause applies, once by the body binding the
variables. The tail is a field, so a byte scanner allocates two tails per step.

Measured on a 5-byte walk of `<<_c, rest :: binary>>` -- four reads per step
for a two-field pattern:

    P DISPATCH read      <- field 0, the integer
    P DISPATCH read      <- field 1, the binary tail
    P BODY read          <- field 0 again
    P BODY read          <- field 1 again

It shows up as exactly 2x the ProcBin stubs: a 640-byte walk allocates 1151
where there are 576 shareable tails.

TWO LOWERINGS OF THE SAME CLAUSE HEAD, both live:

  * SELECTION -- dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs `bitstring_question` builds a
    Region::Bitstring, lowered at jobs/native.rs:3277 to one BitReadField per
    field.
  * BINDING -- jobs/body.rs `lower_bitstring_pattern` lowers the SAME pattern
    into ExprStep::BitstringInit + one ExprStep::BitstringRead per field,
    which becomes LoweredStep -> BackendStep -> Prim::BitReadField at
    jobs/native.rs:1366.

THE SEAM IS ALREADY THERE, HALF-USED. Dispatch records everything it extracted
(`state.bitstring_fields`, `apply_direct_bitstring_bindings`), and
`bitstring_direct_bindings` already names `rest` and `_c` as direct bindings
of those fields -- so the values the body re-reads are in hand when it re-reads
them. `lower_bitstring_pattern` even takes `with_asserts: bool`, and a clause
head the dispatch already decided passes false: the ASSERTS are dropped because
the dispatch made them redundant. The READS are not, though the dispatch made
them redundant in exactly the same way.

DONE = finish the thought `with_asserts` starts. When the dispatch covered the
pattern, bind from what it published instead of re-lowering. What has to be
threaded is the plan's subject ids for the fields, which `bitstring_field_subject`
already computes on both the interp and native sides.

Not runtime work at all -- body lowering learning what the dispatch plan already
knows. Sized as an arc, not a patch. Sibling of fz-5xp.22, instance of
fz-5xp.21. Was the invisible half of fz-5xp.55's cost; now that tails are
shared, these two reads ARE the cost of a scan.

comments.text:
MEASURED PRECISELY, and the description's 'twice' is right but undersells it.

Probing both interp read sites on a 5-byte walk of `<<_c, rest :: binary>>`:

    P DISPATCH read      <- field 0, the integer
    P DISPATCH read      <- field 1, the binary tail
    P BODY read          <- field 0 again
    P BODY read          <- field 1 again        ... x5 steps

FOUR reads per step for a two-field pattern. Each FIELD is read twice: once by
the dispatch plan deciding whether the clause matches, and once by the body
binding the variables. The tail is a field, so that is two tail allocations per
step, which is where the 2x stub count comes from.

THE MECHANISM TO AVOID IT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY POPULATED. Dispatch
stores what it extracted:

    state.bitstring_fields.insert((subject, index), extracted);
    apply_direct_bitstring_bindings(plan, field_subject, extracted, state);

and the native emitter does the same in emit_bitstring_test. So the values the
body re-reads are already in hand at the moment it re-reads them. The body emits
its own BitReadField prims regardless, because the lowering does not know the
dispatch region covered the same pattern.

So this is not a runtime fix. It is the clause head being compiled TWICE -- once
into the dispatch matrix to decide the clause, once into the body to bind -- and
the second one is redundant exactly when the first one covered it. Related to
fz-5xp.22 (fold the two native dispatch region emitters into one) and another
instance of fz-5xp.21.

NEXT STEP: find where body lowering emits BitReadField for a clause-head pattern
and whether it can see that the dispatch plan already projected that subject.
Not attempted yet.

ARCHITECTURE LOCATED. Two lowerings of the same clause head, both live.

  * SELECTION -- dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs `bitstring_question` builds a
    Region::Bitstring, and the lowering at jobs/native.rs:3277 emits a
    BitReadField per field to decide the clause. It already records every field
    it extracted, and `bitstring_direct_bindings` already names `rest` and
    `_c` as direct bindings of those fields.

  * BINDING -- jobs/body.rs `lower_bitstring_pattern` lowers the SAME pattern
    into ExprStep::BitstringInit + one ExprStep::BitstringRead per field, which
    becomes LoweredStep::BitstringRead -> BackendStep::BitstringRead ->
    Prim::BitReadField at jobs/native.rs:1366.

Both run, so each field is read twice and the tail is allocated twice.

THE SEAM IS ALREADY THERE, HALF-USED. `lower_bitstring_pattern` takes
`with_asserts: bool`, and a clause head the dispatch already decided passes
false -- the ASSERTS are dropped because the dispatch made them redundant. The
READS are not, even though the dispatch made them redundant in exactly the same
way and has the values in hand.

So the fix is to finish the thought that `with_asserts` starts: when the
dispatch covered the pattern, bind from what it published rather than
re-lowering the pattern. What has to be threaded is the plan's subject ids for
the fields, which `bitstring_field_subject` already computes on both the interp
and native sides.

NOT A SMALL CHANGE, and it is not runtime work at all -- it is body lowering
learning what the dispatch plan already knows. Sized as an arc, not a patch.
Sibling of fz-5xp.22.

title: A clause head with a bitstring pattern is compiled twice, so every field is read twice
